Trapped In the Deep

By: Graham Coetzer | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Desperate and dying - a group of illegal miners trapped underground in an abandoned mine shaft might finally be saved after a standoff with authorities that lasted months. But is this a rescue or reco

Unique Selling Point:
The group of miners are some of the thousands of illegal artisanal miners who have been working below ground in and around existing mines in the Klerksdorp, Stilfontein and Orkney areas. The current tragedy was set in motion when police, under their Operation Vala Umgodi that has targeted illicit mining across the country. According to sources, there are at least 400 men stuck underground, and they have sent letters to the surface stating 109 of them have died underground. Two videos have been released to the media by a group representing the miners, that seem to show at least three dozen dead bodies and emaciated miners. They claim the miners stuck underground are dying from starvation, because the police aren't allowing food supplies down.

Summary:
Mine Rescue Services, who specialises in these kinds of operations, have arrived at the site and are starting recovery and rescue operations today. A cage will be dropped more than a kilometre below surface, to where the miners currently are. MRS will start with the removal of bodies before the live miners are rescued. SAPS is on site to arrest survivors. If the body count is above 100, it puts this disaster amongst one of the biggest death tolls in mining history in SA. Meanwhile, desperate families arrive at the site every day, unsure of whether their loved ones will emerge from the disaster alive.

This is news story with a some deep human interest elements,

Further information:
In 2014/15 se were at the Buffelsfontein Mine when they were under attack from large groups of illegal miners, we did a whole insert on it then
We have the videos of the dead bodies and miners underground
We have lots of other cellphone videos and images we can use
We can speak to families of miners and community leaders

Extra Budget Items:
Accomodation in Stilfontein for one night for the crew
Fuel expenses to Stilfontein

Trapped in the Deep
Draft Script 2
23 Jan 2025

INTRO

Upsound
cellphone video of shaft, man’s voice calls down.

VO
More than a km below ground, hundreds of men are trapped in the darkness of an abandoned mine shaft.

Upsound
Cellphone video of shaft, voices echo

VO
Harrowing cries for help float to the surface...

The desperate voices of those once seeking their fortunes, now fighting for survival.


Act 1
VO
Stilfontein, a once-thriving gold-mining hub in the North West, is a shadow of its former self. Most of its mines are now aboandoned.

It’s become a ground zero for the escalating illegal mining crisis in our country, as we discovered during an investigation here 10 years ago.

Link Govan
After a decade of illegal mining here, the police finally stepped in with a controversial plan to force out these zama zamas.

VO TIMELINE GFX
Under Operation Vala Umgodi or “close the hole”, police surrounded illegal miners in Stilfontein, cutting off supplies.

By August last year, it was reported miners in Shaft 11 of the old Buffelsfontein mine were now trapped with no food.

Despite this, government adopted a hardline attitude that would later be strongly criticised by activists.

Upsound Minster Khumbudzo Ntshaveni
We are going to smoke them out, they will come out.

VO
Then, last month, a high court ordered that food and water be sent to the trapped miners.

Finally, a little over ten days ago, and after a months-long standoff, a mission was launched to rescue those trapped in Shaft 11.

Link Govan

Hundreds of illegal miners decended here, seeking there fortunes. And they were trapped. Now they’re emerging one by one, some of them in body bags.

VO
It’s become the latest chapter in the country’s illegal mining nightmare – one in which the local community has played a central role.

People here have sent food to the hungry miners, filling a gap left by government’s hardline position. Many here have also been demanding a rescue mission from day one of the crisis.

ACT 2

Link Govan
This is Khuma, the township adjacent to the Buffelsfontein mine. Unemployment here is rife, and the township’s economy is almost entirely dependent on illegal mining. So this isn’t a tragedy happening at an abandoned mineshaft, it’s a tragedy happening right here, in this community.

Upsound Johanna Santho
Govan: Tell me about your son, what’s his name?

Johanna: My son is Isaac Santho.

Govan: Isaac?

Johanna: Yes.

Govan: How old is he?

Johanna: 24 years.

VO
Johanna Santho, known as Mama Joy to many in Khuma, hasn’t seen or heard from her son Isaac since July last year.

That’s when he joined a group of zama zamas underground at Buffelsfontein.

Upsound Johanna
Johanna: Then he saw that he didn’t get the job. Then he ended up saying Mama no, somebody said lets go hustling in the mine.

Govan: He asked you for permission?

Johanna: Yes.

Govan: What did you think?

Johanna: Then I asked him when you get caught, what are you going to do? Because the police are going to arrest you at the mine. He said we’re going to the mine that is not working anymore.


VO
The zamas at shaft 11 used a basic rope and pulley system, like this one for access and supplies.

But that was all interrupted by operation Vala Umgodi .

Mama Joy says police treated the men below like rats.

Upsound Johanna.
Johanna: That’s how Vala Umgodi means. When you’re staying there, and take the gun and standing there, when you knew that the rat is there, obviously when the rat hears he will stay there. He knows that when he comes out, they will kill him, so he will stay. Because of hunger, yes they were there. But there’s nothing that we can say. Only God knows what happened.

Govan: Mama, I can’t imagine what you’re going through. Everyday.

VO
During the siege, over 1,400 illegal miners emerged at Stilfontein’s Margaret Shaft which has a working elevator. They were immediately arrested.

Those trapped 1.3km below ground at Shaft 11 had fewer options.

Upsound Zama
Underground there are these big cockroaches, like the ones in the movies. So others they were eating that. Because there was no food.

VO
This man, who’s asked us to hide his identity, was one of those trapped. Instead of waiting to be rescued, he made a two-and-a-half-hour journey underground to the connected shaft 10.

This cell phone video captured other miners emerging there… again, only to be arrested.

Upsound Zama
Zama: You shake, because you’ve got cramps like your hands are stuck, like you become tired, you can’t move your hands. Then you have to hold that steel, hold that steel and say God please help me. And on our way up we met with nine dead bodies. Nine.

Govan: Nine?

Zama: Some were fresh, some were bones.

VO
Videos taken of the dire conditions below ground caused an outrage. Among the throngs gathered at the surface were activists who argued that many of the trapped miners were clearly too weak to escape.

Upsound Jessica Lawrence
And in the video that we captured on Saturday, the miner that is taking the video counts the dead bodies, and the rows go on.

VO
Jessica Lawrence is from Lawyers for Human Rights.

Upsound Jessica Lawrence 5:15
Govan: What is it that the police did wrong?

Jessica: The method that they chose to adopt, in combating crime, resulted in the slow starvation and dehydration of miners trapped underground.

VO
Also at the surface were members of the local and international media. Many had been reporting on the crisis since it began. Reports were hard to verify, but occasional evidence emerged of the grim reality below.

Upsound Govan
This is a common site around here, pathology vans and ambulances. The pathology vans are coming to collect the bodies, and the ambulances are coming to fetch those who’ve emerged alive. They’re coming up in a frail condition.

VO
The rescue mission followed months of wrangling and legal threats. When it eventually got underway, it was led by Mines Rescue Services, experts in underground rescues. They used a giant mobile winder to lower a steel cage deep underground - An astonishing 26 minutes to get to the trapped men.

UPSOUND CAGE GOES UNDER

VO
Our arrival coincided with a significant lightning storm – an appropriate backdrop for arguably one of the country’s worst ever mining disasters.

Upsound Upsound Maj Gen Patrick Asaneng
You must remember that it is not the government or the police, despite what people are saying. The narrative that is there is that these people were starved to death, but the post mortems are still going to be conducted.

VO
Acting North West Commissioner, Patrick Asaneng, says police complied with the high court order to allow food to be sent underground.

Upsound Upsound Maj Gen Patrick Asaneng
Govan: The police are being accused of having starved these people to death, by blocking other entrances and forcing them into a position where they couldn’t get out?

Asaneng: The issue of food being sent underground was used as a bargaining chip. There are some of the illegal miners who came up and indicated that the food that was sent underground, was hoarded by the ring leaders underground. It was even sold to them. And that is the narrative that is not being told.

Link Govan
The tragedy here at Stilfontein has definitely polarised South Africans, we’re divided. And there seems to be an expectation growing that we should accept illegal miners. But this isn’t a victimless crime. We know that this funds organised crime. And it’s very dangerous, people are killed.

VO
We first reported on the problems at the Buffelsfontein mine a decade ago.

This footage shows more than a 100 zamas in the bush next to the mine. Once they gain access to the property, it’s a free for all as they descend on 10 shaft – the very shaft where miners more recently emerged.

Some of them even armed themselves with weapons and bulletproof vests stolen from security personnel.

We were first hand witnesses to the violence that so often accompanies illegal mining when a patrol vehicle we were in was fired at.

Upsound NW Zamas Insert

Man 1: There he is, there he is, there he is. He’s standing between the trees behind the bush.

Man 2: Is he shooting?

Man 1: Ja. There he’s walking back. Shot, shoot, shoot. Cover you ears.

Man 2: Alright finished, finished.

VO
Even operational mines in Stilfontein aren’t safe. This footage shows armed zamas inside a haulage area used by mine workers.

Pursuing them deep underground is a dangerous challenge…

Upsound Security footage
Man: Check for bombs…

VO
Zamas often boobytrap tunnels and shafts to hamper pursuit.

Upsound Security footage
Explosive detonated

VO
In this case, the team was fortunate to escape with only minor shrapnel injuries.

The improvised explosive devices used were similar to these ones.

Upsound Security footage
Shooting at security

VO
There’s no cover in tunnels like these - When the bullets fly, the only option is to lie flat or hug a wall.

Upsound Security footage
Security return fire

VO
By the third day of the rescue, police announced that all miners still alive in shaft 11, had been safely brought to the surface.

Upsound Maj Gen Patrick Asaneng
This particular operation was a rescue mission. Because you’ll recall that government has been taken to court to say people are trapped underground they don’t have energy to resurface on their own. So as soon as we are done with this, then the operation will be terminated. But not Vala Umgodi.

ACT 3

VO
In total 324 extractions had been done – 78 of those brought to the surface were dead. Only five survivors were South African citizens. The rest were from Lesotho, Mozambique and Zimbabwe. It’s a source of tension in nearby communities.

Upsound Zama
Here in Khuma, where I stay, people who are coming from out of South Africa they are making a lot of money, they are driving big cars. They are building houses. They have access to everything – because of that money of the zama zama.

VO
On our final day in Stilfontein, the media was finally given access to the shaft exit as the cage surfaced one last time—empty, except for the equipment used to confirm no one was left below.

Upsound Govan
There’s something really ominous about this machine. It brings life, and death. And you don’t know until the cage reaches the top of the shaft… Life shattering news for the families.

VO
Mama Joy’s son Isaac was not amongst those rescued. She’ll have to wait for the results of DNA tests to find out if he was one of the deceased.

As the rescuers packed their gear and the media retreated, the cage stood as a stark symbol of lives lost and narrowly saved. As it was dismantled, the extent of this crisis, its consequences, and its lessons would no doubt fade too.

ENDS








PROMOS
Promo 1

Upsound Cage comes to surface

Voice
After the deaths of at least 78 illegal miners in Stilfontein – one question remains. Who’s to blame?

Upsound Jessica Lawrence
They dies as a result of starvation.

Voice
How did a month’s long standoff with authorities result in South Africa’s latest mining disaster?

Upsound
IF NEEDED



Promo 2

Upsound Zama
Then you have to hold that steel, hold that steel and say God please help me.

Voice
After the deaths of at least 78 illegal miners in Stilfontein, we take a closer look at how the tragedy unfolded.

UPS Johanna
Johanna: Because of hunger, yes they were there. But there’s nothing that we can say. Only God knows what happened.


Promo 3
Voice
Deep beneath the earth, the tentacles of organized crime networks.

Upsound Security
Man: Check for bombs…

Voice
But after a controversial plan to smoke out zama zamas in Stilfontein resulted in tragedy, who’s to blame?

Upsound Maj Gen Asaneng
The issue of food being sent underground was used as a bargaining chip.

Upsound Upsound Maj Gen Patrick Asaneng Govan: The police are being accused of having starved these people to death, by blocking other entrances and forcing them into a position where they couldn’t get out? Asaneng: The issue of food being sent underground was used as a bargaining chip. There are some of the illegal miners who came up and indicated that the food that was sent underground, was hoarded by the ring leaders underground. It was even sold to them. And that is the narrative that is not being told. Link Govan The tragedy here at Stilfontein has definitely polarised South Africans, we’re divided. And there seems to be an expectation growing that we should accept illegal miners. But this isn’t a victimless crime. We know that this funds organised crime. And it’s very dangerous, people are killed. VO We first reported on the problems at the Buffelsfontein mine a decade ago. This footage shows more than a 100 zamas in the bush next to the mine. Once they gain access to the property, it’s a free for all as they descend on 10 shaft – the very shaft where miners more recently emerged. Some of them even armed themselves with weapons and bulletproof vests stolen from security personnel. We were first hand witnesses to the violence that so often accompanies illegal mining when a patrol vehicle we were in was fired at. Upsound NW Zamas Insert Man 1: There he is, there he is, there he is. He’s standing between the trees behind the bush. Man 2: Is he shooting? Man 1: Ja. There he’s walking back. Shot, shoot, shoot. Cover you ears. Man 2: Alright finished, finished. VO Even operational mines in Stilfontein aren’t safe. This footage shows armed zamas inside a haulage area used by mine workers. Pursuing them deep underground is a dangerous challenge… Upsound Security footage Man: Check for bombs… VO Zamas often boobytrap tunnels and shafts to hamper pursuit. Upsound Security footage Explosive detonated VO In this case, the team was fortunate to escape with only minor shrapnel injuries. The improvised explosive devices used were similar to these ones. Upsound Security footage Shooting at security VO There’s no cover in tunnels like these - When the bullets fly, the only option is to lie flat or hug a wall. Upsound Security footage Security return fire VO By the third day of the rescue, police announced that all miners still alive in shaft 11, had been safely brought to the surface. Upsound Maj Gen Patrick Asaneng This particular operation was a rescue mission. Because you’ll recall that government has been taken to court to say people are trapped underground they don’t have energy to resurface on their own. So as soon as we are done with this, then the operation will be terminated. But not Vala Umgodi. ACT 3 VO In total 324 extractions had been done – 78 of those brought to the surface were dead. Only five survivors were South African citizens. The rest were from Lesotho, Mozambique and Zimbabwe. It’s a source of tension in nearby communities. Upsound Zama Here in Khuma, where I stay, people who are coming from out of South Africa they are making a lot of money, they are driving big cars. They are building houses. They have access to everything – because of that money of the zama zama. VO On our final day in Stilfontein, the media was finally given access to the shaft exit as the cage surfaced one last time—empty, except for the equipment used to confirm no one was left below. Upsound Govan There’s something really ominous about this machine. It brings life, and death. And you don’t know until the cage reaches the top of the shaft… Life shattering news for the families. VO Mama Joy’s son Isaac was not amongst those rescued. She’ll have to wait for the results of DNA tests to find out if he was one of the deceased. As the rescuers packed their gear and the media retreated, the cage stood as a stark symbol of lives lost and narrowly saved. As it was dismantled, the extent of this crisis, its consequences, and its lessons would no doubt fade too. But there’s nothing that we can say. Only God knows what happened. Promo 3 Voice Deep beneath the earth, the tentacles of organized crime networks. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Desperate and dying - a group of illegal miners trapped underground in an abandoned mine shaft might finally be saved after a standoff with authorities that lasted months. But is this a rescue or reco
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The group of miners are some of the thousands of illegal artisanal miners who have been working below ground in and around existing mines in the Klerksdorp, Stilfontein and Orkney areas. The current tragedy was set in motion when police, under their Operation Vala Umgodi that has targeted illicit mining across the country. According to sources, there are at least 400 men stuck underground, and they have sent letters to the surface stating 109 of them have died underground. Two videos have been released to the media by a group representing the miners, that seem to show at least three dozen dead bodies and emaciated miners. They claim the miners stuck underground are dying from starvation, because the police aren't allowing food supplies down.
metadata.Summary: Mine Rescue Services, who specialises in these kinds of operations, have arrived at the site and are starting recovery and rescue operations today. A cage will be dropped more than a kilometre below surface, to where the miners currently are. MRS will start with the removal of bodies before the live miners are rescued. SAPS is on site to arrest survivors. If the body count is above 100, it puts this disaster amongst one of the biggest death tolls in mining history in SA. Meanwhile, desperate families arrive at the site every day, unsure of whether their loved ones will emerge from the disaster alive. This is news story with a some deep human interest elements,
metadata.Further information: In 2014/15 se were at the Buffelsfontein Mine when they were under attack from large groups of illegal miners, we did a whole insert on it then We have the videos of the dead bodies and miners underground We have lots of other cellphone videos and images we can use We can speak to families of miners and community leaders
